title: Format a date as %m/%d/%Y, %H:%M:%S
description:
Format the current date using this format: "%m/%d/%Y, %H:%M:%S")

Python-Gym adaptation: reading the live clock would make the expected result non-deterministic, so implement as format_datetime(dt), taking a fixed datetime.datetime object dt instead of the real current time, and returning the string produced by formatting dt with "%m/%d/%Y, %H:%M:%S".
starter_code:
import datetime

def format_datetime(dt):
    # your code here
    pass
hints: The datetime module has a method that turns a datetime object into a string according to a format code, the mirror image of strptime.
The format codes you need are %m for month, %d for day, %Y for a 4-digit year, and %H, %M, %S for hour, minute, second.
Use dt.strftime("%m/%d/%Y, %H:%M:%S") to produce the formatted string.
expected_behavior: Given a fixed datetime.datetime object, returns it formatted as a string in %m/%d/%Y, %H:%M:%S form.
explanation: dt.strftime(fmt) builds a string from a datetime object according to the given format codes: %m/%d/%Y produces a zero-padded month/day/4-digit-year date, and %H:%M:%S produces zero-padded 24-hour time, matching the format requested.
